title: Celebrating Chinese New Year
synopsis: Have you ever celebrated Spring Festival in China? In this lesson, we learn how most Chinese people like to spend their lunar New Year’s.

fullText.simplified:
中国人春节喜欢做什么？

    马上就是春节了，也就是中国的新年。中国人喜欢在春节做些什么呢？
    春节前，中国人喜欢把家和办公室打扫干净，然后在门上贴“福”字和一些新年的祝福语。中国人喜欢和爸爸妈妈一起过春节，所以在别的地方工作的人，春节前都会买票回家。
    新年的前一天，也叫“除夕”。在除夕，中国人喜欢和家人一起包饺子，吃饺子。晚上会和家人一起看“春节联欢晚会”，一边看电视，一边给亲人或者朋友发祝福短信。到了晚上12点，大家还会在一起放鞭炮，热热闹闹地迎接新年。
    新年的第一天，也叫“大年初一”。中国人喜欢在大年初一穿上新衣服，到亲人、朋友家里说“新年好”，发红包。
fullText.traditional:
中國人春節喜歡做什麼？

    馬上就是春節了，也就是中國的新年。中國人喜歡在春節做些什麼呢？
    春節前，中國人喜歡把家和辦公室打掃乾淨，然後在門上貼“福”字和一些新年的祝福語。中國人喜歡和爸爸媽媽一起過春節，所以在別的地方工作的人，春節前都會買票回家。
    新年的前一天，也叫“除夕”。在除夕，中國人喜歡和家人一起包餃子，吃餃子。晚上會和家人一起看“春節聯歡晚會”，一邊看電視，一邊給親人或者朋友發祝福短信。到了晚上12點，大家還會在一起放鞭炮，熱熱鬧鬧地迎接新年。
    新年的第一天，也叫“大年初一”。中國人喜歡在大年初一穿上新衣服，到親人、朋友家裡說“新年好”，發紅包。

raw.synopsis: Have you ever celebrated Spring Festival in China? In this lesson, we learn how most Chinese people like to spend their lunar New Year’s.
sentence_translations: What do Chinese people like to do during Spring Festival?
It is soon Spring Festival; in other words the Chinese New Year.
So what do Chinese people like to do during Spring Festival?
Before Spring Festival, Chinese people like to clean up their home and office.
They then stick the character for “good fortune” above their door together with some New Year's blessings.
The Chinese like to spend Spring Festival together with their father and mother, ..
.. so everyone who is out working in other areas buys tickets to go home before Spring Festival.
The day before New Year's is also known as the Lunar New Year's Eve.
On the Lunar New Year's Eve, the Chinese like to make and eat dumplings together with their family.
In the evening, the family watches the “New Year's Gala” together, ..
.. and while watching TV they send text messages of blessings to friends and relatives.
At midnight, everyone is still together setting off fire crackers to welcome the New Year in a lively fashion.
The first day of the New Year is also called the Lunar New Year's Day.
On New Year's Day, Chinese people like to put on new clothes and visit the homes of friends and family to say “Happy New Year” and hand over red envelopes.
